anchor.statement: Lemma 10.4. Let F(t) = ∫︁ t 0 ∥f(s)∥ 2 ds for 0 ≤ t ≤ 1. Then F(1) < ∞ , and ∥u(t)∥ 2 2 + 2 ∫︂ t 0 ∥∇u(s)∥ 2 2 ds ≤ F (t) 2 (0 ≤ t < 1). (10.13) In particular the kinetic energy is uniformly bounded, and the total dissipation on [0, 1) is finite.

correspondence.note: candidate_energy_estimates states F(1) < ∞, (10.13) with factor 2ν, and finite dissipation on [0, 1), for any viscosity and any candidate; its candidate hypothesis includes a uniform energy bound, which uniform_finite_energy derives from the equation for smooth compactly supported fields with zero datum.

sharp inequality on every shorter interval, and its total-dissipation bound.

links.doc:
A smooth compact force yields one uniform bound for the kinetic energy
before time one. The proof includes square integrability at every time, then
uses the PDE-derived energy inequality and a scalar integrating factor.
links.name: NavierStokesR3.CompactEnergy.uniform_finite_energy

      ContDiffOn ℝ (↑⊤) p NavierStokes.ProblemStatement.preSingularDomain →

suggestions.doc:
The dissipation of a paper candidate is integrable in time on the whole
interval before blowup. This is the finite total dissipation conclusion of
Lemma 10.4, in addition to the uniform kinetic-energy bound.
